allowExec.default: true if `api.host` is exposed to network, false otherwise
allowExec.description:
Allow running test files via the API.
If `api.host` is exposed to network and `allowWrite` is true,
anyone connected to the API server can run arbitrary code on your machine.

allowWrite.default: true if `api.host` is exposed to network, false otherwise
allowWrite.description: Allow any write operations from the API server.

allowExternal.description: Collect coverage of files outside the project `root`.

autoAttachSubprocess.description:
Track coverage of the `node:child_process` and `node:worker_threads` spawned during test run.
Supported only by `v8` provider.

changed.description:
Collect coverage only for files changed since a specified commit or branch.
Inherits the default value from `test.changed`.

clean.description: Clean coverage results before running tests

cleanOnRerun.description: Clean coverage report on watch rerun

customProviderModule.description: Name of the module or path to a file to load the custom provider from

enabled.description: Enables coverage collection. Can be overridden using `--coverage` CLI option.

exclude.description:
List of files excluded from coverage as glob patterns.
Files are first checked against `coverage.include`.

See [Including and excluding files from coverage report](https://vitest.dev/guide/coverage.html#including-and-excluding-files-from-coverage-report) for examples.

excludeAfterRemap.description:
Apply exclusions again after coverage has been remapped to original sources.
This is useful when your source files are transpiled and may contain source maps
of non-source files.

Use this option when you are seeing files that show up in report even if they
match your `coverage.exclude` patterns.

htmlDir.description:
Directory of HTML coverage output to be served in UI mode and HTML reporter.
This is automatically configured for builtin reporter with html output (`html`, `html-spa`, and `lcov` reporters).
Use this option to override with custom coverage reporting location.

ignoreClassMethods.description: Set to array of class method names to ignore for coverage

include.description:
List of files included in coverage as glob patterns.
By default only files covered by tests are included.

See [Including and excluding files from coverage report](https://vitest.dev/guide/coverage.html#including-and-excluding-files-from-coverage-report) for examples.

instrumenter.description:
Custom instrumenter factory to use instead of the default `@vitest/istanbul-lib-instrument`.

The factory receives the same runtime coverage options Vitest passes to its
built-in Istanbul instrumenter and must return an object implementing the
`CoverageInstrumenter` interface.

This allows using faster instrumenters (e.g., oxc-coverage-instrument, SWC) while
keeping the Istanbul coverage pipeline for collection, merging, and reporting.

processingConcurrency.description:
Concurrency limit used when processing the coverage results.
Defaults to `Math.min(20, os.availableParallelism?.() ?? os.cpus().length)`

reportOnFailure.description: Generate coverage report even when tests fail.

reporter.description:
Coverage reporters to use.
See [istanbul documentation](https://istanbul.js.org/docs/advanced/alternative-reporters/) for detailed list of all reporters.

reportsDirectory.description: Directory to write coverage report to

skipFull.description: Do not show files with 100% statement, branch, and function coverage

watermarks.description:
Watermarks for statements, lines, branches and functions.

Default value is `[50,80]` for each property.

html.description: The html content for the test.

pretendToBeVisual.description:
jsdom does not have the capability to render visual content, and will act like a headless browser by default.
It provides hints to web pages through APIs such as document.hidden that their content is not visible.

When the `pretendToBeVisual` option is set to `true`, jsdom will pretend that it is rendering and displaying
content.

url.description:
url sets the value returned by window.location, document.URL, and document.documentURI,
and affects things like resolution of relative URLs within the document
and the same-origin restrictions and referrer used while fetching subresources.

userAgent.description: userAgent affects the value read from navigator.userAgent, as well as the User-Agent header sent while fetching subresources.

interopDefault.description: Interpret CJS module's default as named exports

moduleDirectories.description: A list of directories relative to the config file that should be treated as module directories.

optimizer.description: Enable dependency optimization. This can improve the performance of your tests.

transformAssets.description:
Should Vitest process assets (.png, .svg, .jpg, etc) files and resolve them like Vite does in the browser.

These module will have a default export equal to the path to the asset, if no query is specified.

**At the moment, this option only works with `{ pool: 'vmThreads' }`.**

transformCss.description:
Should Vitest process CSS (.css, .scss, .sass, etc) files and resolve them like Vite does in the browser.

If CSS files are disabled with `css` options, this option will just silence UNKNOWN_EXTENSION errors.

**At the moment, this option only works with `{ pool: 'vmThreads' }`.**

transformGlobPattern.description:
Regexp pattern to match external files that should be transformed.

By default, files inside `node_modules` are externalized and not transformed.

**At the moment, this option only works with `{ pool: 'vmThreads' }`.**

prewarm.description:
Called once for every resolved browser project right before its shared
Vite server is created, so the provider can start preparing the browser
(e.g. launching it) concurrently. Optional, fire-and-forget: errors must
surface through the normal provider flow.

async.description: If the script should be loaded asynchronously.

content.description:
JavaScript content to be injected. This string is processed by Vite plugins if type is "module".

You can use `id` to give Vite a hint about the file extension.

id.description:
If "content" is provided and type is "module", this will be its identifier.

If you are using TypeScript, you can add `.ts` extension here for example.

src.description: Path to the script. This value is resolved by Vite so it can be a node module or a file path.

alias.description:
Specifies an `Object`, or an `Array` of `Object`,
which defines aliases used to replace values in `import` or `require` statements.
Will be merged with the default aliases inside `resolve.alias`.

allowOnly.description: Allow tests and suites that are marked as only

api.description:
Serve API options.

When set to true, the default port is 51204.

attachmentsDir.description: Directory path for storing attachments created by `context.annotate`

bail.description: Stop test execution when given number of tests have failed.

browser.description: options for test in a browser environment

chaiConfig.description:
Modify default Chai config. Vitest uses Chai for `expect` and `assert` matches.
https://github.com/chaijs/chai/blob/4.x.x/lib/chai/config.js

changed.description:
Runs tests that are affected by the changes in the repository, or between specified branch or commit hash
Requires initialized git repository

clearMocks.description: Will call `.mockClear()` on all spies before each test

css.description:
Indicates if CSS files should be processed.

When excluded, the CSS files will be replaced with empty strings to bypass the subsequent processing.

dangerouslyIgnoreUnhandledErrors.description: Ignore any unhandled errors that occur

deps.description: Handling for dependencies inlining or externalizing

detectAsyncLeaks.description: Detect asynchronous resources leaking from the test file.

diff.description: Path to a module which has a default export of diff config.

dir.description: Base directory to scan for the test files

disableConsoleIntercept.description:
By default, Vitest intercepts console output during tests to add context such as the test file and test title.
In browser mode, this interception is required to forward logs from the browser DevTools to the terminal.
It is also required for console log previews in the Vitest UI.
Disabling console interception can be useful when you want to debug code with normal synchronous terminal logging.

env.description: Custom environment variables assigned to `process.env` before running tests.

environment.description:
Running environment

Supports 'node', 'jsdom', 'happy-dom', 'edge-runtime'

If used unsupported string, will try to load the package `vitest-environment-${env}`

execArgv.description:
Pass additional arguments to `node` process when spawning the worker.

See [Command-line API | Node.js](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest/api/cli.html) for more information.

Set to `process.execArgv` to pass all arguments of the current process.

Be careful when using, it as some options may crash worker, e.g. --prof, --title. See https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/41103

expandSnapshotDiff.description: Show full diff when snapshot fails instead of a patch.

requireAssertions.description: Throw an error if tests don't have any expect() assertions.

diagnostics.description:
Print performance hints after the run when the collected timings show
that a configuration change would make the run significantly faster.
Hints are never printed for options that were set explicitly.

Set to `false` to disable all hints, or disable them individually:
- `isolate`: hint when `isolate: true` spends a significant amount of
  time spawning a fresh worker (and re-creating the environment) for
  every test file, estimating how much `isolate: false` could save.
- `environment`: hint when re-creating a DOM environment for every test
  file dominates the run and a `vm` pool would set it up once per worker.
- `import`: hint when test files repeatedly evaluate the same module
  graph (typical for barrel-file imports) and `isolate: false` would
  evaluate it once per worker.
- `transform`: hint when transforming modules dominates the run and
  `fsModuleCache` would persist the results across runs.

importDurations.description:
Configure import duration collection and display.

The `limit` option controls how many imports to collect and display.
The `print` option controls CLI terminal output.
UI can always toggle the breakdown display regardless of `print` setting.

failOnDanger.description:
Fail the test run if any import exceeds the danger threshold.
When failing, the breakdown is always printed regardless of `print` setting.

limit.description: Maximum number of imports to collect and display.

print.description:
When to print import breakdown to CLI terminal after tests finish.
- `true`: Always print
- `false`: Never print (default)
- `'on-warn'`: Print only when any import exceeds the warn threshold

thresholds.description: Duration thresholds in milliseconds for coloring and warnings.

danger.description: Danger threshold - imports exceeding this are shown in red.

warn.description: Warning threshold - imports exceeding this are shown in yellow/orange.

nodeLoader.description:
If module runner is disabled, Vitest uses a module loader to transform files to support
`import.meta.vitest` and `vi.mock`.

If you don't use these features, you can disable this.

This option only affects `loader.load` method, Vitest always defines a `loader.resolve` to populate the module graph.

preParse.description:
Parse test specifications before running them.
This will apply `.only` flag and test name pattern across all files without running them.

vcsProvider.description:
Custom provider for detecting changed files. Used with the `--changed` flag
to determine which files have been modified.

By default, Vitest uses Git to detect changed files. You can provide a custom
implementation of the `VCSProvider` interface to use a different version control system.

viteModuleRunner.description:
Controls whether Vitest uses Vite's module runner to run the code or fallback to the native `import`.

If Node.js cannot process the code, consider registering [module loader](https://nodejs.org/api/module.html#customization-hooks) via `execArgv`.

fileParallelism.description:
Should all test files run in parallel. Doesn't affect tests running in the same file.
Setting this to `false` will override `maxWorkers` option to `1`.

forceRerunTriggers.description:
Glob pattern of file paths that will trigger the whole suite rerun

Useful if you are testing calling CLI commands

fsModuleCache.description:
Cache transformed modules on the file system and reuse them between reruns
and separate Vitest processes, which can significantly speed up cold starts.

fsModuleCachePath.description:
Directory where the {@link fsModuleCache} is stored. Can be set per project;
projects that don't override it fall back to the root's cache directory.

By default the cache is stored inside `node_modules` at the workspace root, so
that it is naturally invalidated when dependencies are reinstalled.

hookTimeout.description: Default timeout of a hook in milliseconds

include.description: A list of [glob patterns](https://superchupu.dev/tinyglobby/comparison) that match your test files.

includeSource.description: Include globs for in-source test files

includeTaskLocation.description: Include "location" property inside the test definition

injectCjsGlobals.description:
Inject CommonJS module variables (`module`, `exports`, `require`,
`__filename`, `__dirname`) into every module processed by Vitest.

When disabled, ES modules no longer have access to CommonJS variables,
matching how the code runs outside of Vitest. Modules detected to be
CommonJS keep these variables because they are part of the module scope.
The module type is detected the same way Node.js does it: the file
extension wins, then the `type` field in the nearest package.json,
then the presence of ESM syntax in the file.

This option doesn't affect externalized modules which are always
executed by the native runtime.

inspect.description:
Debug tests by opening `node:inspector` in worker / child process.
Provides similar experience as `--inspect` Node CLI argument.

Requires `fileParallelism: false`.

inspectBrk.description:
Debug tests by opening `node:inspector` in worker / child process and wait for debugger to connect.
Provides similar experience as `--inspect-brk` Node CLI argument.

Requires `fileParallelism: false`.

inspector.description: Inspector options. If `--inspect` or `--inspect-brk` is enabled, these options will be passed to the inspector.

waitForDebugger.description: Wait for debugger to connect before running tests

isolate.description:
Run tests in an isolated environment. This option has no effect on vmThreads pool.

Disabling this option improves performance if your code doesn't rely on side effects.

logHeapUsage.description: Show heap usage after each test. Useful for debugging memory leaks.

maxConcurrency.description: A number of tests that are allowed to run at the same time marked with `test.concurrent`.

maxWorkers.description: Maximum number or percentage of workers to run tests in.

mockReset.description: Will call `.mockReset()` on all spies before each test

name.description: Name of the project. Will be used to display in the reporter.

onConsoleLog.description:
Custom handler for console.log in tests.

Return `false` to ignore the log.

onStackTrace.description:
Enable stack trace filtering. If absent, all stack trace frames
will be shown.

Return `false` to omit the frame.

onUnhandledError.description: A callback that can return `false` to ignore an unhandled error

outputFile.description:
Write test results to a file when the --reporter=json` or `--reporter=junit` option is also specified.
Also definable individually per reporter by using an object instead.

pool.description:
Pool used to run tests in.

Supports 'threads', 'forks', 'vmThreads', 'vmForks'

projects.description:
Options for projects.

When a project is referenced as a config file (or a directory with one) and
that config declares `projects` itself, it becomes a container: it doesn't
run tests, only provides the projects it declares. Inline configurations
cannot declare `projects`.

provide.description: Define variables that will be returned from `inject` in the test environment.

repeats.description: Repeat every test a specific number of times regardless of the result.

reporters.description:
Custom reporter for output. Can contain one or more built-in reporter names, reporter instances,
and/or paths to custom reporters.

restoreMocks.description: Will call `.mockRestore()` on all spies before each test

retry.description:
Retry configuration for tests.
- If a number, specifies how many times to retry failed tests
- If an object, allows fine-grained retry control

⚠️ WARNING: Function form is NOT supported in a config file
because configurations are serialized when passed to worker threads.
Use the function form only in test files directly.

runner.description: Path to a custom test runner.

sequence.description: Options for configuring the order of running tests.

dump.description:
The folder where Vitest stores the contents of transformed
test files that can be inspected manually.

If `true`, Vitest dumps the files in `.vitest-dump` folder relative to the root of the project.

You can also use `VITEST_DEBUG_DUMP` env variable to enable this.

load.description:
If dump is enabled, should Vitest load the files from there instead of transforming them.

You can also use `VITEST_DEBUG_LOAD_DUMP` env variable to enable this.

sharedViteServer.description:
Let inline projects that don't modify the Vite config reuse the Vite
server of the config that declares them. Instead of resolving a new
Vite config and creating a new server per project, such projects share
the server and its transform cache.

A project still gets its own server when it defines Vite-level options
(`plugins`, `resolve`, ...) or test options that affect the
Vite config: `alias`, `browser`, `css`, `deps.moduleDirectories`,
`deps.optimizer`, `mode`, `root`,
or when `extends` doesn't point to the declaring config.

This option is only respected in the root configuration.

silent.description:
Silent mode

Use `'passed-only'` to see logs from failing tests only.

slowTestThreshold.description: The number of milliseconds after which a test is considered slow and reported as such in the results.

snapshotEnvironment.description: Path to a custom snapshot environment module that has a default export of `SnapshotEnvironment` object.

strictTags.description: Should Vitest throw an error if test has a tag that is not defined in the config.

tags.description:
Define tags available in your test files.

If test defines a tag that is not listed here, an error will be thrown.

taskTitleValueFormatTruncate.description:
Sets length limit for formatted values interpolated into generated task titles.

This affects values inserted by APIs like `test.each` and `test.for`.

teardownTimeout.description: Default timeout to wait for close when Vitest shuts down, in milliseconds

testNamePattern.description: Run test names with the specified pattern

testTimeout.description: Default timeout of a test in milliseconds

typecheck.description: Options for configuring typechecking test environment.

unstubEnvs.description: Will restore all env stubs to their original values before each test

unstubGlobals.description: Will restore all global stubs to their original values before each test

vmMemoryLimit.description:
Specifies the memory limit for `worker_thread` or `child_process` before they are recycled.
If you see memory leaks, try to tinker this value.

watchTriggerPatterns.description:
Pattern configuration to rerun only the tests that are affected
by the changes of specific files in the repository.

LinkMapper.description: maps report nodes to output paths, see the html report's `linkMapper` option

enabled.description:
Enable Vitest trace view artifacts collection.

This option controls Vitest's own trace-view pipeline, independently from provider-specific trace retention.

inlineImages.description: Inline loaded `` element pixels in trace view snapshots. This uses rrweb's image inlining support. It improves offline replay for still images, but can increase trace artifact size and does not preserve original image resource bytes.

recordCanvas.description:
Capture canvas pixels in trace view snapshots.

This uses rrweb's canvas snapshot support and can increase trace artifact size.
In the trace viewer, this enables a weaker replay iframe sandbox because rrweb needs scripts to redraw canvas data.

Specifies an `Object`, or an `Array` of `Object`,
which defines aliases used to replace values in `import` or `require` statements.
Will be merged with the default aliases inside `resolve.alias`.

When set to true, the default port is 51204.

groupOrder.description:
Controls the order in which this project runs its tests when using multiple [projects](/guide/projects).

- Projects with the same group order number will run together, and groups are run from lowest to highest.
- If you don’t set this option, all projects run in parallel.
- If several projects use the same group order, they will run at the same time.

hooks.description:
Defines how hooks should be ordered
- `stack` will order "after" hooks in reverse order, "before" hooks will run sequentially
- `list` will order hooks in the order they are defined
- `parallel` will run hooks in a single group in parallel

setupFiles.description:
Defines how setup files should be ordered
- 'parallel' will run all setup files in parallel
- 'list' will run all setup files in the order they are defined in the config file

callToJSON.description:
Call `toJSON` on objects before formatting them.
Ignored after the formatter has already called `toJSON` once for a value.

escapeRegex.description: Whether to escape special characters in regular expressions.

escapeString.description: Whether to escape special characters in strings.

highlight.description: Whether to highlight syntax using terminal colors.

indent.description: Number of spaces to use for each level of indentation.

maxDepth.description: Maximum depth to recurse into nested values.

maxOutputLength.description:
Approximate per-depth-level budget for output length.
When the accumulated output at any single depth level exceeds this value,
further nesting is collapsed. This is a heuristic safety valve, not a hard
limit — total output can reach up to roughly `maxDepth × maxOutputLength`.

maxWidth.description: Maximum number of items to print in arrays, sets, maps, and similar collections.

min.description:
Whether to minimize added whitespace, including indentation and line breaks.

When `true`, pretty-format defaults `spacingInner` to `' '`, `spacingOuter` to `''`,
and ignores indentation. It also changes the default for `printBasicPrototype`
from `true` to `false`, although an explicit `printBasicPrototype` still wins.
Explicit `spacingInner` / `spacingOuter` overrides still apply.

printBasicPrototype.description:
Whether to print `Object` / `Array` prefixes for plain objects and arrays.

Defaults to `true`, unless `min` is `true`, in which case it defaults to `false`.
An explicit `printBasicPrototype` value always overrides the `min` default.

printFunctionName.description: Whether to include the function name when formatting functions.

printShadowRoot.description: Whether to include shadow-root contents when formatting DOM nodes.

quoteKeys.description:
Whether to always quote object property keys.

For example:
`{"a": 1}` when `true`
`{a: 1}` when `false` and the key is a valid identifier
`{"my-key": 1}` still stays quoted because it is not a valid identifier

singleQuote.description:
Whether to print strings using single quotes instead of double quotes.

For example:
`"hello"` when `false`
`'hello'` when `true`

spacingInner.description:
Whitespace inserted after commas between items or entries.

For example, in `{a: 1, b: 2}` or `[1, 2]`, this controls the gap after each comma:
`{a: 1,${spacingInner}b: 2}`
`[1,${spacingInner}2]`

Defaults to `'\n'` in regular mode and `' '` when `min` is `true`.
Can be overridden independently of `min`.

spacingOuter.description:
Whitespace inserted immediately inside collection/object delimiters.

For example, this controls the space or newline right after the opening delimiter
and right before the closing delimiter:
`{${spacingOuter}a: 1${spacingOuter}}`
`[${spacingOuter}1${spacingOuter}]`

Defaults to `'\n'` in regular mode and `''` when `min` is `true`.
Can be overridden independently of `min`.

workspacePath.description:

allowJs.description:
Check JS files that have `@ts-check` comment.
If you have it enabled in tsconfig, this will not overwrite it.

checker.description: What tools to use for type checking.

enabled.description: Run typechecking tests alongside regular tests.

exclude.description: Pattern for files that should not be treated as test files

ignoreSourceErrors.description: Do not fail, if Vitest found errors outside the test files.

include.description: Pattern for files that should be treated as test files

only.description: When typechecking is enabled, only run typechecking tests.

spawnTimeout.description: Minimum time in milliseconds it takes to spawn the typechecker.

tsconfig.description: Path to tsconfig, relative to the project root.

outputDir.description:
Directory used as the report artifact root.

The report entry is written to `<outputDir>/index.html` and the UI
implementation files live under `<outputDir>/ui/`. By default this is the
shared `.vitest` artifact directory.

singleFile.description: Inline report assets, metadata, and attachments into the generated HTML file.

addFileAttribute.description: Add <testcase file="..."> attribute (validated on CIRCLE CI and GitLab CI)

ancestorSeparator.description:
Separator used to join ancestor describe block names when building the
`{classname}` template variable (and the default testcase name when
{@link titleTemplate} is not set).

classnameTemplate.description:
Template for the `classname` attribute of `<testcase>`.

Can be a template string or a function.

Supported placeholders:
- `{filename}` – relative path from root (e.g. `src/foo.test.ts`)
- `{filepath}` – absolute file path
- `{basename}` – file name without directory (e.g. `foo.test.ts`)
- `{classname}` – ancestor describe names joined by {@link ancestorSeparator}
- `{title}` – leaf test title
- `{suitename}` – top-level describe block name
- `{displayName}` – Vitest project name

hostname.description: Hostname to use in the report. By default, it uses os.hostname()

stackTrace.description: Include stack traces in test failure reports.

stdout.description:
Print the report to stdout instead of writing it to a file.
Ignored when {@link outputFile} is set.

suiteNameTemplate.description:
Template for the `name` attribute of `<testsuite>`.

Can be a template string or a function.

Supported placeholders:
- `{title}` – first top-level describe name (falls back to file basename)
- `{filename}` – relative path from root
- `{filepath}` – absolute file path
- `{basename}` – file basename
- `{displayName}` – Vitest project name

When not set the relative file path from root is used (current default behaviour).

titleTemplate.description:
Template for the `name` attribute of `<testcase>`.

Can be a template string or a function. Supports the same placeholders as
{@link classnameTemplate}.

When not set the full test title including ancestor describe hierarchy is used
(current default behaviour, e.g. `outer > inner > test name`).

stdout.description:
Print the report to stdout instead of writing it to a file.
Ignored when {@link outputFile} is set.

perFile.description:
Check thresholds per file. When set to an object, the top-level thresholds
still apply to the aggregate and every file must additionally meet these
per-file minimums.

Can also be set per glob pattern via `thresholds['<glob>'].perFile`. Glob
patterns do not inherit this top-level `perFile`; set it on each glob
explicitly.

condition.description:
Condition to determine if a test should be retried based on the error.
- If a RegExp, it is tested against the error message
- If a function, called with the TestError object; return true to retry

NOTE: Functions can only be used in test files, not in vitest.config.ts,
because the configuration is serialized when passed to worker threads.

count.description: The number of times to retry the test if it fails.

delay.description: Delay in milliseconds between retry attempts.

Retry.description:
Retry configuration for tests.
Can be a number for simple retry count, or an object for advanced retry control.

groupOrder.description:
Controls the order in which this project runs its tests when using multiple [projects](/guide/projects).

- Projects with the same group order number will run together, and groups are run from lowest to highest.
- If you don’t set this option, all projects run in parallel.
- If several projects use the same group order, they will run at the same time.

hooks.description:
Defines how hooks should be ordered
- `stack` will order "after" hooks in reverse order, "before" hooks will run sequentially
- `list` will order hooks in the order they are defined
- `parallel` will run hooks in a single group in parallel

seed.description: Seed for the random number generator.

sequencer.description:
Class that handles sorting and sharding algorithm.
If you only need to change sorting, you can extend
your custom sequencer from `BaseSequencer` from `vitest/node`.

setupFiles.description:
Defines how setup files should be ordered
- 'parallel' will run all setup files in parallel
- 'list' will run all setup files in the order they are defined in the config file

files.description:
Should files run in random order. Long running tests will not start
earlier if you enable this option.

tests.description: Should tests run in random order.

shuffle.description: Should files and tests run in random order.

external.description:
Externalize means that Vite will bpass the package to native Node.

Externalized dependencies will not be applied Vite's transformers and resolvers.
And does not support HMR on reload.

Typically, packages under `node_modules` are externalized.

fallbackCJS.description: Try to guess the CJS version of a package when it's invalid ESM

inline.description:
Vite will process inlined modules.

This could be helpful to handle packages that ship `.js` in ESM format (that Node can't handle).

If `true`, every dependency will be inlined

Summarizers.description: names of the summarizer strategies supported by {@link SummarizerFactory}

autoUpdate.description:
Update threshold values automatically when current coverage is higher than earlier thresholds
Also can accept a function to format the new threshold values

perFile.description:
Check thresholds per file. When set to an object, the top-level thresholds
still apply to the aggregate and every file must additionally meet these
per-file minimums.

Can also be set per glob pattern via `thresholds['<glob>'].perFile`. Glob
patterns do not inherit this top-level `perFile`; set it on each glob
explicitly.

onBrowserInit.description:
Called when the project initiated the browser instance.
project.browser will always be defined.

onHookEnd.description: Called after the hook finished running.

onHookStart.description: Called before the hook starts to run.

onTestCaseAnnotate.description: Called when annotation is added via the `task.annotate` API.

onTestCaseArtifactRecord.description: Called when artifacts are recorded on tests via the `recordArtifact` utility.

onTestCaseReady.description:
Called when test case is ready to run.
Called before the `beforeEach` hooks for the test are run.

onTestCaseResult.description:
Called after the test and its hooks are finished running.
The `result()` cannot be `pending`.

onTestModuleCollected.description: Called when the test file is loaded and the module is ready to run tests.

onTestModuleEnd.description: Called when all tests of the test file have finished running.

onTestModuleQueued.description: Called when the module is enqueued for testing. The file itself is not loaded yet.

onTestModuleStart.description: Called when starting to run tests of the test file

onTestRunEnd.description: Called when the test run is finished.

onTestRunStart.description: Called when the new test run starts.

onTestSuiteReady.description:
Called when test suite is ready to run.
Called before the `beforeAll` hooks for the test are run.

onTestSuiteResult.description:
Called after the test suite and its hooks are finished running.
The `state` cannot be `pending`.

condition.description:
Condition to determine if a test should be retried based on the error.
Must be a RegExp tested against the error message.

count.description: The number of times to retry the test if it fails.

delay.description: Delay in milliseconds between retry attempts.

bi.description:
Serializable retry configuration (used in config files).
Functions cannot be serialized, so only string conditions are allowed.

extends.description:
Relative path to the extendable config. All other options will be merged with this config.
If `true`, the project will inherit all options from the root config.
Set to `false` to keep the project configuration completely separate from the root config.

concurrent.description:
Whether suites and tests run concurrently.
Tests inherit `concurrent` from `describe()` and nested `describe()` will inherit from parent's `concurrent`.

description.description: A description for the tag. This will be shown in the CLI help and UI.

fails.description: Whether the test is expected to fail. If it does, the test will pass, otherwise it will fail.

meta.description: Custom test metadata available to reporters.

name.description: The name of the tag. This is what you use in the `tags` array in tests.

only.description: Should this test be the only one running in a suite.

priority.description:
Priority for merging options when multiple tags with the same options are applied to a test.

Lower number means higher priority. E.g., priority 1 takes precedence over priority 3.

repeats.description:
How many times the test will run again.
Only inner tests will repeat if set on `describe()`, nested `describe()` will inherit parent's repeat by default.

retry.description:
Retry configuration for the test.
- If a number, specifies how many times to retry
- If an object, allows fine-grained retry control

skip.description: Whether the test should be skipped.

todo.description: Whether the test should be skipped and marked as a todo.

exclude.description: Exclude globs for benchmark test files

include.description: Include globs for benchmark test files

includeSource.description: Include globs for in-source benchmark test files

provider.description:
The benchmark provider that executes registered benchmarks and produces
their results. Provide a path to a module whose default export implements
`BenchmarkProvider`. The path is resolved relative to the project
root. If not specified, the built-in provider is used.

retainSamples.description:
Include `samples` array of benchmark results for API or custom reporter usages.
This is disabled by default to reduce memory usage.

suppressExportGetterWarnings.description: Disable warnings when a benchmark accesses module export getters too many times.

commands.description:
Commands that will be executed on the server
via the browser `import("vitest/browser").commands` API.

connectTimeout.description: Timeout for connecting to the browser

dependencySourcemaps.description:
Serve sourcemaps of your dependencies (files in `node_modules`) to the
browser during headless test runs.

These sourcemaps are used by browser devtools: when disabled, pausing
inside dependency code shows the compiled code the browser actually
runs instead of the dependency's original sources. If you don't debug
into your dependencies this way, disabling them makes test runs faster:
the server doesn't generate and inline the maps, and every browser tab
downloads several times fewer bytes.

Reported test errors are not affected: stack frames pointing into a
pre-bundled dependency are mapped using the sourcemaps stored on disk
even when this option is disabled.

Vitest never serves sourcemaps of its own pre-built modules in headless
runs (unless `--inspect` is used) — their frames are hidden from stack
traces anyway. Sourcemaps of your own source files are always served.

detailsPanelPosition.description:
Default position for the details panel in browser mode
'right' shows the details panel on the right side (horizontal split)
'bottom' shows the details panel at the bottom (vertical split)

enabled.description: if running tests in the browser should be the default

errorFormat.description: Format used for locator "Cannot find element" error details.

exact.description: Should locators match the text exactly by default

testIdAttribute.description: Attribute used to locate elements by test id

orchestratorScripts.description: Scripts injected into the main window.

screenshotDirectory.description:
Directory where screenshots will be saved when page.screenshot() is called
If not set, all screenshots are saved to __screenshots__ directory in the same folder as the test file.
If this is set, it will be resolved relative to the project root.

screenshotFailures.description: Should Vitest take screenshots if the test fails

testerHtmlPath.description: Path to the index.html file that will be used to run tests.

screenshots.description: Whether to capture screenshots during tracing. Screenshots are used to build a timeline preview.

snapshots.description:
If this option is true tracing will
- capture DOM snapshot on every action
- record network activity

tracesDir.description:
The directory where all traces will be stored. By default, Vitest
stores all traces in `__traces__` folder close to the test file.

trace.description:
Generate traces that can be viewed on https://trace.playwright.dev/

This option is supported only by **playwright** provider.

traceView.description:
Enable Vitest trace view artifacts collection.

This option controls Vitest's own trace-view pipeline, independently from provider-specific trace retention.

trackUnhandledErrors.description:
Enables tracking uncaught errors and exceptions so they can be reported by Vitest.

If you need to hide certain errors, it is recommended to use [`onUnhandledError`](https://vitest.dev/config/onunhandlederror) option instead.

Disabling this will completely remove all Vitest error handlers, which can help debugging with the "Pause on exceptions" checkbox turned on.

allowOnly.description: Allow tests and suites that are marked as only

attachmentsDir.description: Directory path for storing attachments created by `context.annotate`

bail.description: Stop test execution when given number of tests have failed.

chaiConfig.description:
Modify default Chai config. Vitest uses Chai for `expect` and `assert` matches.
https://github.com/chaijs/chai/blob/4.x.x/lib/chai/config.js

changed.description:
Runs tests that are affected by the changes in the repository, or between specified branch or commit hash
Requires initialized git repository

clearMocks.description: Will call `.mockClear()` on all spies before each test

css.description:
Indicates if CSS files should be processed.

When excluded, the CSS files will be replaced with empty strings to bypass the subsequent processing.

detectAsyncLeaks.description: Detect asynchronous resources leaking from the test file.

diff.description: Path to a module which has a default export of diff config.

dir.description: Base directory to scan for the test files

disableConsoleIntercept.description:
By default, Vitest intercepts console output during tests to add context such as the test file and test title.
In browser mode, this interception is required to forward logs from the browser DevTools to the terminal.
It is also required for console log previews in the Vitest UI.
Disabling console interception can be useful when you want to debug code with normal synchronous terminal logging.

env.description: Custom environment variables assigned to `process.env` before running tests.

execArgv.description:
Pass additional arguments to `node` process when spawning the worker.

See [Command-line API | Node.js](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest/api/cli.html) for more information.

Set to `process.execArgv` to pass all arguments of the current process.

Be careful when using, it as some options may crash worker, e.g. --prof, --title. See https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/41103

expandSnapshotDiff.description: Show full diff when snapshot fails instead of a patch.

requireAssertions.description: Throw an error if tests don't have any expect() assertions.

diagnostics.description:
Print performance hints after the run when the collected timings show
that a configuration change would make the run significantly faster.
Hints are never printed for options that were set explicitly.

Set to `false` to disable all hints, or disable them individually:
- `isolate`: hint when `isolate: true` spends a significant amount of
  time spawning a fresh worker (and re-creating the environment) for
  every test file, estimating how much `isolate: false` could save.
- `environment`: hint when re-creating a DOM environment for every test
  file dominates the run and a `vm` pool would set it up once per worker.
- `import`: hint when test files repeatedly evaluate the same module
  graph (typical for barrel-file imports) and `isolate: false` would
  evaluate it once per worker.
- `transform`: hint when transforming modules dominates the run and
  `fsModuleCache` would persist the results across runs.

importDurations.description:
Configure import duration collection and display.

The `limit` option controls how many imports to collect and display.
The `print` option controls CLI terminal output.
UI can always toggle the breakdown display regardless of `print` setting.

failOnDanger.description:
Fail the test run if any import exceeds the danger threshold.
When failing, the breakdown is always printed regardless of `print` setting.

limit.description: Maximum number of imports to collect and display.

print.description:
When to print import breakdown to CLI terminal after tests finish.
- `true`: Always print
- `false`: Never print (default)
- `'on-warn'`: Print only when any import exceeds the warn threshold

thresholds.description: Duration thresholds in milliseconds for coloring and warnings.

danger.description: Danger threshold - imports exceeding this are shown in red.

warn.description: Warning threshold - imports exceeding this are shown in yellow/orange.

nodeLoader.description:
If module runner is disabled, Vitest uses a module loader to transform files to support
`import.meta.vitest` and `vi.mock`.

If you don't use these features, you can disable this.

This option only affects `loader.load` method, Vitest always defines a `loader.resolve` to populate the module graph.

preParse.description:
Parse test specifications before running them.
This will apply `.only` flag and test name pattern across all files without running them.

vcsProvider.description:
Custom provider for detecting changed files. Used with the `--changed` flag
to determine which files have been modified.

By default, Vitest uses Git to detect changed files. You can provide a custom
implementation of the `VCSProvider` interface to use a different version control system.

viteModuleRunner.description:
Controls whether Vitest uses Vite's module runner to run the code or fallback to the native `import`.

If Node.js cannot process the code, consider registering [module loader](https://nodejs.org/api/module.html#customization-hooks) via `execArgv`.

fileParallelism.description:
Should all test files run in parallel. Doesn't affect tests running in the same file.
Setting this to `false` will override `maxWorkers` option to `1`.

fsModuleCache.description:
Cache transformed modules on the file system and reuse them between reruns
and separate Vitest processes, which can significantly speed up cold starts.

fsModuleCachePath.description:
Directory where the {@link fsModuleCache} is stored. Can be set per project;
projects that don't override it fall back to the root's cache directory.

By default the cache is stored inside `node_modules` at the workspace root, so
that it is naturally invalidated when dependencies are reinstalled.

hookTimeout.description: Default timeout of a hook in milliseconds

include.description: A list of [glob patterns](https://superchupu.dev/tinyglobby/comparison) that match your test files.

includeSource.description: Include globs for in-source test files

includeTaskLocation.description: Include "location" property inside the test definition

injectCjsGlobals.description:
Inject CommonJS module variables (`module`, `exports`, `require`,
`__filename`, `__dirname`) into every module processed by Vitest.

When disabled, ES modules no longer have access to CommonJS variables,
matching how the code runs outside of Vitest. Modules detected to be
CommonJS keep these variables because they are part of the module scope.
The module type is detected the same way Node.js does it: the file
extension wins, then the `type` field in the nearest package.json,
then the presence of ESM syntax in the file.

This option doesn't affect externalized modules which are always
executed by the native runtime.

inspector.description: Inspector options. If `--inspect` or `--inspect-brk` is enabled, these options will be passed to the inspector.

waitForDebugger.description: Wait for debugger to connect before running tests

isolate.description:
Run tests in an isolated environment. This option has no effect on vmThreads pool.

Disabling this option improves performance if your code doesn't rely on side effects.

errorFormat.description: Format used for locator "Cannot find element" error details.

exact.description: Should locators match the text exactly by default

testIdAttribute.description: Attribute used to locate elements by test id

logHeapUsage.description: Show heap usage after each test. Useful for debugging memory leaks.

maxConcurrency.description: A number of tests that are allowed to run at the same time marked with `test.concurrent`.

maxWorkers.description: Maximum number or percentage of workers to run tests in.

mockReset.description: Will call `.mockReset()` on all spies before each test

onUnhandledError.description: A callback that can return `false` to ignore an unhandled error

provide.description: Define variables that will be returned from `inject` in the test environment.

repeats.description: Repeat every test a specific number of times regardless of the result.

restoreMocks.description: Will call `.mockRestore()` on all spies before each test

retry.description:
Retry configuration for tests.
- If a number, specifies how many times to retry failed tests
- If an object, allows fine-grained retry control

⚠️ WARNING: Function form is NOT supported in a config file
because configurations are serialized when passed to worker threads.
Use the function form only in test files directly.

screenshotDirectory.description:
Directory where screenshots will be saved when page.screenshot() is called
If not set, all screenshots are saved to __screenshots__ directory in the same folder as the test file.
If this is set, it will be resolved relative to the project root.

screenshotFailures.description: Should Vitest take screenshots if the test fails

snapshotEnvironment.description: Path to a custom snapshot environment module that has a default export of `SnapshotEnvironment` object.

strictTags.description: Should Vitest throw an error if test has a tag that is not defined in the config.

tags.description:
Define tags available in your test files.

If test defines a tag that is not listed here, an error will be thrown.

taskTitleValueFormatTruncate.description:
Sets length limit for formatted values interpolated into generated task titles.

This affects values inserted by APIs like `test.each` and `test.for`.

testTimeout.description: Default timeout of a test in milliseconds

testerHtmlPath.description: Path to the index.html file that will be used to run tests.

unstubEnvs.description: Will restore all env stubs to their original values before each test

unstubGlobals.description: Will restore all global stubs to their original values before each test

vmMemoryLimit.description:
Specifies the memory limit for `worker_thread` or `child_process` before they are recycled.
If you see memory leaks, try to tinker this value.
